description.value: Monarch Mountain/A Xéegi Deiyi Conservancy is a BC Parks–managed protected area located immediately east of Atlin in northern BC, on the traditional territory of the Taku River Tlingit First Nation. The 5.3 km Monarch Mountain Trail—the most popular trail in the Atlin region—climbs from a trailhead on Warm Bay Road to summit views and culturally significant lakes used for spiritual activities. The conservancy also permits snowshoeing in winter and wildlife viewing throughout the summer.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is a BC Parks page for Monarch Mountain/A Xéegi Deiyi Conservancy, confirming the OSM URL and that the conservancy is active and open. The site describes a 5.3 km hiking trail accessed from a pull-out on Warm Bay Road near Atlin, with no mention of developed infrastructure such as bike parking, washrooms, or potable water. None of the required cycling-service amenities are confirmed, as the conservancy is a backcountry natural area accessed from a roadside trailhead.

No phone number associated with this specific conservancy; BC Parks general contact is 1-800-689-9025 and parkinfo@gov.bc.ca.
No developed facilities (washrooms, water, bike parking) are mentioned on the BC Parks page for this conservancy.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is an undeveloped backcountry conservancy with a roadside trailhead pull-out — no verified cyclist amenities (bike parking, water, washrooms) and no business infrastructure to service touring cyclists. It may warrant inclusion as a scenic destination attraction for the Atlin area, but the lack of any confirmed WWC-relevant amenities means it should be reviewed against directory inclusion thresholds.
enrichment_extras.notes: The conservancy is culturally significant to the Taku River Tlingit First Nation; the summit plateau lakes are used for spiritual activities and visitors are asked to give users plenty of space.
